The '''1956 FA Charity Shield''' was the 34th [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]], an annual [[association football|football]] match held between the winners of the previous season's [[Football League First Division|Football League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. The match was contested by [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who had won the [[1955–56 Football League First Division|1955–56 Football League]], and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], who had won the [[1955–56 FA Cup]], at [[Maine Road]], [[Manchester]], on 24 October 1956. Manchester United won the match 1–0, with [[Dennis Viollet]] scoring the winning goal. United goalkeeper [[David Gaskell]] made his debut for the club during the game, taking the place of injured goalkeeper [[Ray Wood]], and, at the age of 16 years and 19 days, became the youngest player ever to play for the club.

This game was the first competitive floodlit [[Manchester derby]].<ref>Steve Cawley & Gary James, ''The Pride of Manchester – A History of the Manchester Derby'' (ACL & Polar Publishing, 1991), p 320.</ref> The game was a break with tradition as Charity Shield matches were typically played at the home ground of the league champions, but as Old Trafford had yet to install lights, the game was played at Maine Road. Prior to this, the first floodlit Manchester derby was played on 26 February 1889 at the Belle Vue Athletic Ground. The match was played in aid of the Hyde Coal Mine disaster.<ref>Gary James & Keith Mellor, ''From Maine Men To Banana Citizens'' (Temple Press, 1989), p 8.</ref>
